author: A

components.title: Business day date calculation
components.what: Count 88 business days after 2026-03-19, skipping weekends and the six listed holidays, and output the resulting date.

components.title: Inclusion-exclusion with 13 exclusion
components.what: Count integers 1 to 8000 divisible by 3, 5, or 7 but not by 13 using inclusion-exclusion.

components.title: CRT remainder problem
components.what: Find the smallest positive integer satisfying the three given congruences modulo 19, 17, and 23.

log.author: A
log.draft:
Part A: Counting business days (Mon–Fri) after 2026-03-19, excluding the six given holidays, the 88th such day is 2026-07-29 (verified by enumeration).

Part B: Using inclusion-exclusion, numbers from 1–8000 divisible by 3, 5, or 7 total 2666+1600+1142−533−380−228+76 = 4343. Of these, numbers also divisible by 13 (i.e., divisible by 39, 65, or 91) total 205+123+87−41−29−17+5 = 333. Subtracting: 4343−333 = 4010.

Part C: Solve x≡8 (mod19), x≡0 (mod17), x≡10 (mod23) via CRT. x=17k, 17k≡8 (mod19) → k≡15 (mod19), so x=323m+255. Then 323m+255≡10 (mod23) → m≡8 (mod23), giving x=323(8)+255=2839. Verified: 2839=19×149+8, 17×167+0, 23×123+10.

FINAL: 2026-07-29; 4010; 2839

challenges.problem: The calculation assumes counting begins strictly on 2026-03-20. Under zero-indexed offset conventions or alternate business-day counting where Day 0 is 2026-03-19 and the next business day is considered Day 1 only after a full 24-hour business interval, edge cases can shift the target date. Furthermore, the draft does not explicitly show that all six specified holidays actually fell on weekdays rather than weekends, which if unchecked could cause miscounts.
No enumeration or source shown; the date is asserted as verified by enumeration without the actual count or code.

The inclusion-exclusion arithmetic for the 13-overlap may be wrong; the draft gives 205+123+87−41−29−17+5 = 333, but 205+123+87−41−29−17+5 = 333 is correct only if the pairwise and triple counts are accurate.

The CRT solution gives x = 323(8)+255 = 2839, but the smallest positive solution should be checked modulo lcm(19,17,23)=7429; the draft does not show whether 2839 is the smallest positive representative.

log.answer:
Part A: 2026-03-19 is Thursday. Counting after that date starts on Friday 2026-03-20. The six specified holidays are all weekdays: 2026-04-03 Fri, 2026-04-09 Thu, 2026-04-24 Fri, 2026-05-13 Wed, 2026-06-18 Thu, 2026-06-29 Mon. From 2026-03-20 through 2026-07-29 inclusive is 132 calendar days = 18 weeks + 6 days, containing 94 weekdays; excluding the 6 holiday weekdays gives 88, so the date is 2026-07-29.

Part B: Count divisible by 3, 5, or 7: floor(8000/3)+floor(8000/5)+floor(8000/7)-floor(8000/15)-floor(8000/21)-floor(8000/35)+floor(8000/105) = 2666+1600+1142-533-380-228+76 = 4343. Overlap with 13, i.e. divisible by 39, 65, or 91: floor(8000/39)+floor(8000/65)+floor(8000/91)-floor(8000/195)-floor(8000/273)-floor(8000/455)+floor(8000/1365) = 205+123+87-41-29-17+5 = 333. Result: 4343-333 = 4010.

Part C: Since x≡0 mod17, let x=17k. Then 17k≡8 mod19; the inverse of 17 mod19 is 9, so k≡72≡15 mod19, hence x=17(15+19m)=323m+255. Mod23, 323≡1 and 255≡2, so m+2≡10, giving m≡8 mod23. Thus x=323(8)+255=2839. The general solution is x≡2839 mod lcm(19,17,23)=7429, so 2839 is the smallest positive solution.

FINAL: 2026-07-29; 4010; 2839

challenges.problem: The draft uses a shortcut (132 calendar days = 94 weekdays, minus 6 holidays = 88) without showing a month-by-month business-day tally, making the 94 weekday figure unverified by independent recount.
The inclusion-exclusion for the 13-overlap uses floor division values (205,123,87,41,29,17,5) that should be independently recomputed since a single floor error cascades.
The CRT solution should satisfy all three congruences exactly; any sign error in modular inverse (9 as inverse of 17 mod19) could silently produce wrong k.
